## 1. Import Packages

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

## 2. Read and Inspect Data

Let's load the parkrun dataset included in `00_data/ParkRunPerformanceData.xlsx` and inspect summary statistics:

```{python}
parkrun = pd.read_excel("00_data/ParkRunPerformanceData.xlsx", sheet_name="Sheet1")
parkrun.columns = ["date", "runtime"]

print(parkrun.head())
parkrun[["date", "runtime"]].describe()
```

## 3. Visualise the Data

We can plot the distribution and trend of runtimes over time using `seaborn` and `matplotlib`:

```{python}
#| label: fig-runtime-trend-py
#| fig-cap: "Parkrun runtimes over time in Python."
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
sns.scatterplot(data=parkrun, x="date", y="runtime", alpha=0.75, ax=ax)
ax.set_title("Parkrun Runtimes Over Time")
ax.set_xlabel("Event Date")
ax.set_ylabel("Run Time (minutes)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
